result.summary: /workspace/verifiers/parsers/{parser.py,think_parser.py,xml_parser.py,__init__.py} are byte-identical to upstream v0.1.3.post0 (`diff -u` against /tmp/vfrepo is empty for all four), and all parser tests pass. Functionally the only outright spec violation is XMLParser: it omits the documented `extract_fn` parameter and never calls `super().__init__()`, so instances have no `.logger` and no `.extract_fn` (upstream fixed this in 0.1.4). Everything else is (a) an empty `verifiers/parsers/__init__.py` that makes `from verifiers.parsers import XMLParser` fail, (b) the spec-demanded "detailed docstrings" being absent on ~8 public methods, and (c) small crash-on-edge-case robustness gaps; I verified in scratch copies (/tmp/s3, /tmp/s4, /tmp/s5) that every fix below keeps all 156 tests passing.

findings.detail: Spec documents `XMLParser(Parser): __init__(fields, answer_field="answer", extract_fn=...)`. Current signature is `def __init__(self, fields, answer_field: str = "answer"):` with no `extract_fn` and no `super().__init__(...)` call anywhere in the body, so Parser.__init__ never runs. Verified at runtime: `XMLParser(['reasoning','answer'])` -> `hasattr(p,'logger') == False`, `hasattr(p,'extract_fn') == False`; `XMLParser(['a'], extract_fn=lambda x: x)` -> `TypeError: XMLParser.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'extract_fn'`. This is the one real API divergence from the documented signature; upstream fixed it in 0.1.4 (`super().__init__(extract_fn=extract_fn)` immediately after the docstring) and kept it through 0.3.0. It also makes XMLParser the only Parser subclass without `.logger`, so any code doing `self.logger.warning(...)` on an XMLParser (e.g. the upstream 'think' field warning, or user rubrics/envs) raises AttributeError.
findings.recommendation:
Add the third parameter and the super() call (exact upstream 0.1.4 form; verified 156/156 pass in /tmp/s4):

    def __init__(
        self,
        fields: list[str | tuple[str, ...]],
        answer_field: str = "answer",
        extract_fn: Callable[[str], str] = lambda x: x,
    ):
        """...existing docstring..."""
        super().__init__(extract_fn=extract_fn)
        # list of (canonical, [alternatives])
        self._fields: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []

`Callable` is already imported at xml_parser.py:3. Optionally also accept `**kwargs` and forward them (`super().__init__(extract_fn=extract_fn, **kwargs)`) for parity with this repo's `Parser(**kwargs)`/`ThinkParser(**kwargs)` extension - also verified 156/156 - but extract_fn alone is the minimal spec-satisfying change.
findings.title: XMLParser.__init__ omits documented extract_fn and never calls super().__init__() (no self.logger, no self.extract_fn)

findings.detail: The file is 0 bytes. `python -c "from verifiers.parsers import XMLParser"` -> `ImportError: cannot import name 'XMLParser' from 'verifiers.parsers'`. Only fully-qualified module paths work (`from verifiers.parsers.xml_parser import XMLParser`), which is what all in-repo call sites use. Top-level `verifiers/__init__.py` does export all three (lines importing .parsers.parser/.think_parser/.xml_parser plus `__all__`), so the spec's `verifiers/__init__.py` requirement is met; the subpackage-level export surface is not. Upstream leaves this file empty in every version 0.1.3-0.3.0, so this is a spec-vs-upstream judgement call, but adding it is free and strictly widens the API.
findings.recommendation:
Write the three re-exports into verifiers/parsers/__init__.py (verified no circular-import problem, 156/156 pass in /tmp/scratch_ws):

    """Parsers for extracting structured content from model rollouts."""

    from verifiers.parsers.parser import Parser
    from verifiers.parsers.think_parser import ThinkParser
    from verifiers.parsers.xml_parser import XMLParser

    __all__ = ["Parser", "ThinkParser", "XMLParser"]
findings.title: verifiers/parsers/__init__.py is empty: `from verifiers.parsers import Parser/XMLParser/ThinkParser` raises ImportError

findings.detail: The spec requires docstrings documenting input/output formats and data types. AST audit of the four files shows: no module docstring in any of parser.py / think_parser.py / xml_parser.py / __init__.py; `Parser.__init__` (parser.py:16), `Parser.parse` (parser.py:22) and `Parser.parse_answer` (parser.py:43) have NO docstring at all; `ThinkParser` class (think_parser.py:7), `ThinkParser.__init__` (:8) and `ThinkParser.parse` (:12) have NO docstring; `XMLParser` class (xml_parser.py:9) has NO class docstring. The docstrings that do exist are one-liners with no Args/Returns/type information (`get_assistant_messages`/`get_system_messages`/`get_user_messages`/`get_tool_messages` at parser.py:25-41, `XMLParser.parse_answer` at :81, `get_format_str` at :102, `get_fields` at :228). The `Parser` class docstring at parser.py:8-14 is also stale: it advertises "`get_final_answer` returns the last message's content" but the method is named `parse_answer` (upstream corrected this wording in 0.1.6).
findings.recommendation: Add Google-style docstrings (docstring-only edits cannot affect tests). Minimum set: (1) module docstrings for all four files; (2) `Parser.__init__`: document `extract_fn: Callable[[str], str]` applied by `parse`, and that `**kwargs` are set as arbitrary instance attributes; (3) `Parser.parse`: "Args: text (str). Returns: Any - `extract_fn(text)`; subclasses may return a structured object."; (4) `Parser.parse_answer`: "Args: completion (Messages = str | list[ChatMessage]). Returns: str | None. For str completions parses the whole string; for chat completions parses the LAST message's `content`."; (5) the four `get_*_messages`: "Args: completion (list[ChatMessage]). Returns: list[ChatMessage] - messages whose `role` == '<role>', in order."; (6) `get_format_reward_func`: "Returns: Callable[[list[ChatMessage], ...], float] in [0.0, 1.0]; base implementation always returns 1.0."; (7) `ThinkParser` class + `parse`: document that text up to and including the last `</think>` is dropped, that missing `</think>` yields `""`, and that `extract_fn` is then applied to the stripped remainder; (8) `XMLParser` class docstring describing the `fields` schema (str = fixed tag, tuple = canonical name + aliases, every alias becomes an attribute on the returned SimpleNamespace), `answer_field`, and the ValueError/TypeError contract. Also fix `get_final_answer` -> `parse_answer` in the Parser class docstring (parser.py:13).
findings.title: Public parser methods lack the detailed input/output docstrings the spec demands

findings.detail: `format_reward_func` computes `sum(...) / len(messages)` with no empty guard, so `ThinkParser().get_format_reward_func()([{'role':'user','content':'x'}])` raises `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` (verified). tests/test_think_parser.py:136-150 (`test_format_reward_function_no_assistant_messages`) deliberately wraps the call in `try/except (ZeroDivisionError, IndexError)` and accepts either outcome, so returning 0.0 satisfies it. A reward func that raises is only survivable because `Rubric.call_reward_func` swallows exceptions and substitutes 0.0 while logging an error (verifiers/rubrics/rubric.py:100-108) - the reward is the same, but every such rollout emits a spurious ERROR log. Upstream added the guard in 0.3.0.
findings.recommendation:
In think_parser.py, inside `format_reward_func`, add the guard before the division:

        def format_reward_func(completion: list[ChatMessage], **kwargs) -> float:
            messages = self.get_assistant_messages(completion)
            if not messages:
                return 0.0
            return sum(follows_format(m["content"]) for m in messages) / len(messages)  # type: ignore

Verified 156/156 pass in /tmp/scratch_ws; the tolerant test now takes the `0.0 <= reward <= 1.0` branch.
findings.title: ThinkParser format reward func raises ZeroDivisionError when a completion has no assistant messages

findings.detail: tests/test_xml_parser.py:148-150 explicitly documents `XMLParser([])` as supported ("Empty fields is actually allowed"). But the returned reward func unconditionally indexes `self._fields[0][1]` (xml_parser.py:186-188) and `self._fields[-1][1]` (:196-198), so `XMLParser([]).get_format_reward_func()([{'role':'assistant','content':'hi'}])` raises `IndexError: list index out of range` (verified). Same class of latent issue: `expected_field_count = len(self._fields)` would be a division by zero at :207 if `has_any_field` could ever be true with no fields. Separately, the inner `format_reward_func` is declared `def format_reward_func(completion: list[ChatMessage]):` with no `**kwargs` and no return annotation, unlike Parser's and ThinkParser's - it happens to work only because `Rubric.call_reward_func` filters kwargs to the signature when there is no VAR_KEYWORD (rubric.py:102-104), so it breaks any caller that invokes it directly with extra keyword args.
findings.recommendation:
Widen the guard at xml_parser.py:125-129 and normalize the inner signature:

        def format_reward_func(completion: list[ChatMessage], **kwargs) -> float:
            """Reward function that checks if each step follows the expected format."""
            model_messages = self.get_assistant_messages(completion)
            if not model_messages or not self._fields:
                return 0.0

Verified 156/156 pass in /tmp/s3; `bad_reward == 0.2` for the non-empty-schema case in test_format_reward_function is unaffected.
findings.title: XMLParser.get_format_reward_func raises IndexError for a parser built with an empty field list

findings.detail: `return self.parse(completion[-1]["content"])` (parser.py:47) has two failure modes, both verified: `Parser().parse_answer([])` -> `IndexError: list index out of range`; `Parser().parse_answer([{'role':'assistant','tool_calls':[]}])` -> `KeyError: 'content'`. Both are reachable: MultiTurnEnv.rollout returns an empty `completion` list when `is_completed` is true on the first loop iteration (verifiers/envs/multiturn_env.py:70-73), and ToolEnv-style assistant messages may carry only `tool_calls`. The spec's return type is `str | None`, which the current code can never actually produce for chat input. Note also that it reads the last message of ANY role rather than the last assistant message; upstream changed to last-assistant in 0.1.6+, but v0.1.3.post0 is authoritative here so that semantic change is NOT recommended (I verified it also passes 156/156 in /tmp/s2, but it is a gratuitous behaviour divergence).
findings.title: Parser.parse_answer crashes on empty completions and on messages without a 'content' key

findings.detail: The str branch calls `self.parse(completion, last=True)` (xml_parser.py:84) - tests/test_xml_parser.py:87-91 asserts it returns the LAST `<answer>` in the string. The chat branch calls `self.parse(msg["content"])` with the default `last=False` (:93), so within a single assistant message containing two answer tags it returns the FIRST. Verified: `XMLParser(['reasoning','answer']).parse_answer([{'role':'assistant','content':'<answer>44</answer> x <answer>45</answer>'}])` -> `'44'`, while the same text as a str completion -> `'45'`. The existing test only exercises one answer tag per message so it does not catch the inconsistency. The chat branch also uses `msg["content"]`, which KeyErrors on tool-call-only assistant messages.
findings.recommendation:
Make the chat branch consistent with the "Extract the last answer from a completion" contract in its own docstring (xml_parser.py:82):

            for msg in reversed(self.get_assistant_messages(completion)):
                parsed = self.parse(str(msg.get("content", "")), last=True)

Verified 156/156 pass in /tmp/s3 (test_parse_answer_from_completion still returns '43').
findings.title: XMLParser.parse_answer uses last=True for str completions but not for chat completions

findings.detail: `seen` only ever receives `canonical` (xml_parser.py:44-46), so an alias colliding with another field's tag is accepted silently: `XMLParser([('a','b'), 'b'])` constructs fine, and `parse()` then writes `results['b']` twice (xml_parser.py:76-78), with the later field's match silently overwriting the earlier one. The spec calls for a duplicate-field ValueError; the existing test only covers the canonical case (`XMLParser(['field1','field1'])`, test_xml_parser.py:152-153).
findings.title: XMLParser duplicate-field detection only checks canonical names, not tuple aliases

findings.detail: The capture pattern `rf"<{alt}>\s*(.*?)\s*</{alt}>"` (xml_parser.py:68) already consumes surrounding whitespace, so `strip=False` is a no-op - tests/test_xml_parser.py:67-75 asserts exactly that (`result_no_strip.answer == 'spaced content'  # regex already strips whitespace`). Consequently `has_correct_spacing` in the format reward func (xml_parser.py:163-168) compares `parse(content)` against `parse(content, strip=False)`, which are always identical, so the +0.2 spacing bonus is always granted - and tests/test_xml_parser.py:167-171 hard-asserts `bad_reward == 0.2` for a completion containing no XML at all. Making `strip=False` actually preserve whitespace (e.g. removing `\s*` from the pattern) breaks both assertions. Also note `alt` is interpolated into the regex unescaped, so field names containing regex metacharacters misbehave; upstream has the same limitation.
findings.recommendation: No change. Leave xml_parser.py:68 and the has_correct_spacing block (xml_parser.py:150-168 and the `format_score += 0.2` at :210-211) exactly as they are, and do not escape/alter the tag regex - the 0.2 baseline reward is load-bearing for the existing suite.
findings.title: TRAP - do not 'fix' XMLParser.parse(strip=False) or the has_correct_spacing logic

result.summary: /workspace/verifiers/rubrics/ is byte-for-byte upstream v0.1.3.post0 (only rubric.py's class docstring has been expanded locally), so all six files are internally consistent and the 156 tests pass. Two spec-documented parameters are genuinely absent — `example_id` on `call_reward_func`/`score_rollout` and `example_ids`/`use_tqdm` on `score_rollouts` — and the docstring at rubric.py:33 already advertises `example_id` that the code cannot accept. Separately, `RubricGroup` has no `score_rollout` override, so scoring a rollout through a group injects the group's own default `Parser` instead of each contained rubric's parser (verified: reward 0.0 where it should be 1.0); upstream fixed this in 0.1.4 and added a test for it. I implemented and validated every recommendation below in a /tmp copy: all 156 workspace tests still pass, the upstream 0.1.4 parser test now passes, and `test_call_reward_func_with_var_kwargs` still returns exactly 6.

findings.title: call_reward_func does not accept the spec-documented example_id parameter
findings.detail: The spec signature is `call_reward_func(func, prompt, completion, answer, state, task="default", info=None, example_id=None, **kwargs)`. The current signature (rubric.py:84-94) has no `example_id`; passing it lands in `**kwargs` and is then merged into `merged` unconditionally, which would hand a 7th kwarg to every `(completion, **kwargs)` reward function and break tests/test_rubric.py::TestRubric::test_call_reward_func_with_var_kwargs (asserts exactly 6). Upstream 0.1.6 added `example_id` to `common` unconditionally and had to change that very test to `assert result == 7`, which the hard constraint forbids here. Also note rubric.py:33 (the locally expanded docstring) already documents `example_id: int (index of the source dataset example, when available)` as an accepted reward-func parameter, so the contract is documented but unimplemented. `grep -rn example_id /workspace/verifiers` returns nothing.
findings.recommendation:
Add `example_id: int | None = None,` after `info: Info | None = None,` in the signature (line 92), then inject it into the call dict ONLY when the reward function names it explicitly. Right after `merged = {**common, **kwargs}` (line 116) insert:

```python
        # only surface example_id to reward functions that explicitly name it, so
        # that (**kwargs)-only reward functions keep receiving the documented set
        if "example_id" in sig.parameters:
            merged["example_id"] = example_id
```

Do NOT put `example_id=example_id` inside the `common = dict(...)` literal. Because `example_id` is now a named parameter of `call_reward_func`, it can never leak in via `**kwargs`, so a `(completion, **kwargs)` func still sees exactly 6 kwargs even when the caller passes `example_id=3` (verified: 6.0). A func declaring `(completion, example_id, **kwargs)` receives example_id bound plus 6 kwargs; a func declaring `(completion, example_id)` receives it via the existing `allowed` filter (verified: 7 and 11 respectively).

findings.title: score_rollout does not accept or forward example_id
findings.detail: Spec: `async score_rollout(prompt, completion, answer, state, task="default", info=None, example_id=None, **kwargs) -> RolloutScore`. Current signature (rubric.py:144-153) stops at `info`, and neither the parallel branch (rubric.py:159-168) nor the serial branch (rubric.py:175-184) forwards an example id to `call_reward_func`. Any environment-side interleaved-scoring path built to the spec (`self.rubric.score_rollout(..., example_id=example_id_i, ...)` as in upstream 0.1.6 environment.py:633-642) would silently dump example_id into `**kwargs` and, through the fix above, still not reach reward functions that name it.
findings.recommendation: Add `example_id: int | None = None,` after `info: Info | None = None,` (line 151) and add `example_id=example_id,` to the `self.call_reward_func(...)` call in BOTH the `parallelize_scoring` branch (after `info=info,` at line 166) and the serial branch (after `info=info,` at line 182). No other change; do not add the 0.1.4+ `state["timing"]["scoring_ms"]` bookkeeping — workspace tests pass bare `state={}` and it would raise KeyError.

findings.title: score_rollouts lacks example_ids and use_tqdm
findings.detail: Spec: `async score_rollouts(prompts, completions, answers, states, tasks, infos, example_ids=None, max_concurrent=-1, use_tqdm=True, **kwargs) -> RolloutScores`. Current signature (rubric.py:200-210) is `(..., infos, max_concurrent=-1, **kwargs)`; there is no `example_ids` (so no id can ever reach reward functions) and no `use_tqdm` — `from tqdm.asyncio import tqdm_asyncio` at rubric.py:222 is unconditional, so a tqdm bar is always printed even when the caller (e.g. Environment.generate(use_tqdm=False) per spec) asks for silence, and `use_tqdm=False` passed by a spec-compliant environment would currently leak into `**kwargs` and be handed to every var-kwargs reward function.

findings.title: RubricGroup has no score_rollout override, so contained rubrics' parsers are ignored
findings.detail: RubricGroup overrides get_reward_func_names/funcs/weights and score_rollouts, but not score_rollout. Scoring one rollout therefore falls through to Rubric.score_rollout, which iterates the aggregated `get_reward_funcs()` but calls `self.call_reward_func`, so `self.class_objects["parser"]` — the GROUP's default `Parser()` created in Rubric.__init__ — is injected instead of each contained rubric's parser. Reproduced on the current tree: a Rubric with `XMLParser(fields=["answer"], answer_field="answer")` wrapped in a RubricGroup scores `<answer>42</answer>` vs answer "42" as reward 0.0 with the reward func receiving a plain `Parser`; the same call on a Rubric directly gives 1.0. This is exactly what upstream fixed in 0.1.4 (which also added tests/test_rubric_group.py::test_rubric_group_score_rollout_uses_rubric_parser, asserting `recorded_parsers == [xml_parser]`). I ran that upstream test verbatim: it FAILS on /workspace today and PASSES with the fix below. It also affects any per-rubric class object, e.g. JudgeRubric's judge/judge_client.
findings.recommendation:
Add a score_rollout override that delegates to each rubric (so each uses its own class_objects/parser) and sums rewards and same-named metrics. Insert after add_reward_func (rubric_group.py:46) and extend the type import on line 2 to include `RolloutScore`:

```python
    async def score_rollout(
        self,
        prompt: Messages,
        completion: Messages,
        answer: str,
        state: State,
        task: str = "default",
        info: Info | None = None,
        example_id: int | None = None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> RolloutScore:
        total_reward = 0.0
        aggregated_metrics: dict[str, float] = {}
        for rubric in self.rubrics:
            score = await rubric.score_rollout(
                prompt,
                completion,
                answer,
                state,
                task,
                info,
                example_id=example_id,
                **kwargs,
            )
            total_reward += score.reward
            for key, value in score.metrics.items():
                aggregated_metrics[key] = aggregated_metrics.get(key, 0.0) + value
        return RolloutScore(reward=total_reward, metrics=aggregated_metrics)
```

This matches upstream 0.1.4/0.1.6 and keeps duplicate-name metric summing consistent with score_rollouts (verified: two rubrics with same-named funcs returning 1.0 and 2.0 give `{'dup': 3.0}`, reward 3.0, identical to the score_rollouts path).

findings.title: RubricGroup.score_rollouts passes max_concurrent positionally — becomes example_ids once the new signature lands
findings.detail: rubric_group.py:62-71 calls `rubric.score_rollouts(prompts, completions, answers, states, tasks, infos, max_concurrent, **kwargs)` with `max_concurrent` as the 7th POSITIONAL argument. As soon as `example_ids` is inserted as the 7th parameter of Rubric.score_rollouts (per the spec order), this silently binds an int to `example_ids` and leaves `max_concurrent=-1`: concurrency capping is lost and `list(range(len(prompts)))` is replaced by an int, which then blows up in `zip`. This is an argument-shift landmine created by the otherwise-correct signature change, so the two edits must land together. RubricGroup.score_rollouts also needs its own `example_ids`/`use_tqdm` parameters to satisfy the spec (RubricGroup.score_rollouts is documented as "same as Rubric").
findings.recommendation:
In RubricGroup.score_rollouts: add `example_ids: list[int] | None = None,` before `max_concurrent: int = -1,` (line 49) and `use_tqdm: bool = True,` after it; add `if example_ids is None: example_ids = list(range(len(prompts)))` immediately before `all_scores = RolloutScores(...)`; and change the delegated call to use keywords:

```python
            rubric_scores = await rubric.score_rollouts(
                prompts,
                completions,
                answers,
                states,
                tasks,
                infos,
                example_ids=example_ids,
                max_concurrent=max_concurrent,
                use_tqdm=use_tqdm,
                **kwargs,
            )
```

Use `example_ids=` as a keyword rather than upstream 0.1.6's positional form: a contained rubric that overrides score_rollouts with the old signature then fails loudly instead of silently swallowing the id list as `max_concurrent`. Verified end to end: `group.score_rollouts(..., example_ids=[42], use_tqdm=False)` delivers 42 to the reward func, and `max_concurrent=1` still caps concurrency.

findings.title: Environment.generate/evaluate never supply example_ids, so ids will always fall back to the positional index
findings.detail: This is the integration half of the example_id feature (owned by the envs area, recorded here because the rubric signature is the contract). environment.py:426-435 calls `self.rubric.score_rollouts(prompts=..., completions=..., answers=..., states=..., tasks=..., infos=..., max_concurrent=..., apply_weights=True)` — all keywords, so the new signature is backward compatible and nothing breaks — but no `example_ids` is passed and `GenerateInputs`/`GenerateOutputs` (verifiers/verifiers/types.py:49-69) have no `example_id` field, so `example_id` will always be `list(range(len(prompts)))`, i.e. the flat rollout index, not the source dataset example index. The spec requires `format_dataset` to emit an `example_id` column and `Environment.generate` to carry it.
findings.recommendation: Once `example_id` exists on GenerateInputs/GenerateOutputs (and format_dataset emits the column, with rollouts_per_example duplication preserving the source example index), pass it through as a keyword: `example_ids=results.example_id,` in the environment.py:426 call, and `example_id=example_id_i` in any per-rollout interleaved `score_rollout` call. Keep every argument keyword-only at these call sites so future signature growth cannot shift positions. Optionally add `example_id: int | None = None,` to `EnvGroupRubric.score_rollout` (verifiers/verifiers/envs/env_group.py:44-47) and forward it explicitly at env_group.py:69-71 for readability — it already works via `**kwargs`, so this is cosmetic.

findings.title: score_rollouts silently truncates rollouts when example_ids length mismatches
findings.detail: With the recommended `zip(prompts, ..., example_ids)`, a caller passing a short `example_ids` list silently drops rollouts instead of erroring: verified `score_rollouts(3 prompts, example_ids=[0])` returns `reward=[1.0]` — one score for three rollouts, and the environment then assigns a 1-element reward list to a 3-element batch. Upstream shares this hazard (it uses the same unguarded zip), so it is not a spec deviation, just a cheap robustness win.
findings.recommendation:
Guard right after the default is materialized, before building `zipped`:

```python
        if len(example_ids) != len(prompts):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Number of example_ids ({len(example_ids)}) must match "
                f"number of prompts ({len(prompts)})"
            )
```

No current caller passes a mismatched list, so this is inert for the existing suite; skip it if strict upstream parity is preferred over failing fast.

result.summary: Every Python file in environments/ (20 packages) and examples/ (11 GRPO scripts + sft.py) was statically checked against the API actually implemented in /workspace/verifiers/: all `from verifiers ...` imports, all `vf.*` attribute accesses, all constructor kwargs, all GRPOConfig/GRPOTrainer fields, all Environment-subclass abstract methods, and all reward-function signatures resolve correctly — there are zero references to non-existent APIs, and the docs/ and README code blocks are clean too (the whole area is byte-identical to upstream v0.1.3.post0, so nothing has drifted from the core package). What the area does contain is four independently-verified functional defects that a name-resolution check cannot catch, all caused by `Rubric.call_reward_func` swallowing exceptions into a silent 0.0 or by argparse/env-id mistakes: simpleqa and continuation_quality always score exactly 0.0 because `rubric.judge(...)` is never awaited, examples/sft.py crashes on a duplicate `-g` flag, and train_arc_1d.py loads the wrong module. Separately, the spec requirement to ship "typical use cases and evaluation scripts" for Parser/Rubric/SingleTurnEnv is unmet: examples/ contains only GPU training scripts that need torch/trl/vllm plus a live vLLM server, so nothing demonstrates parsing, reward calculation, or evaluation on the base install. None of the recommendations below touch tests/ or verifiers/, and tests/ never imports environments/ or examples/, so all 156 tests keep passing.

findings.title: No usage/evaluation example scripts exist — explicit spec requirement is unmet
findings.file: examples/ (directory; add examples/eval_gsm8k.py, examples/parsing_and_rewards.py, examples/multiturn_and_tools.py, examples/README.md)
findings.detail: The spec requires the repo to "provide typical use cases and evaluation scripts demonstrating how to use classes such as Parser, Rubric, and SingleTurnEnv for parsing, reward calculation, environment interaction, and evaluation". examples/ contains only 11 GRPO training scripts under examples/grpo/ plus examples/sft.py. Every one of them requires the `train` extra (torch, trl, vllm, accelerate, peft, wandb) AND a separately-launched vLLM server AND multiple GPUs; each starts with `vf.get_model_and_tokenizer(...)` and ends in `trainer.train()`. Not one demonstrates Parser or Rubric in isolation, and not one performs an evaluation. The only evaluation path shipped is the `vf-eval` console script (verifiers/scripts/eval.py), which is a CLI that requires an already-pip-installed environment package plus a live OpenAI-compatible endpoint — it is not a readable example of the Python API. docs/source/*.md and README.md contain illustrative snippets, but several are deliberate non-parsing fragments (e.g. README.md:178-194 shows a `def __init__` with no body), so they are not runnable and cannot be verified. Net result: a user who runs `pip install -e .` (base install, no torch) has zero executable examples. I confirmed the proposed replacement works: I built the eval script outlined below in /tmp and ran it end-to-end against the current /workspace/verifiers, and it printed `reward: [1.2, 1.2]`, `metrics: {'correct_answer': [...], 'format_reward_func': [...]}` and a make_dataset result with columns ['prompt','completion','answer','task','reward','correct_answer','format_reward_func'].
findings.recommendation:
Add three small scripts plus a README. Name them so pytest never collects them (must NOT match `test_*.py`; pyproject sets python_files=["test_*.py"] and testpaths=["tests"], so any non-test-prefixed name in examples/ is safe).

1) `examples/parsing_and_rewards.py` — NO network, runs on the base install. Sections: (a) `Parser()` / `Parser(extract_fn=vf.extract_boxed_answer)` showing `parse`, `parse_answer`, `get_assistant_messages`; (b) `XMLParser(fields=["think", "answer"], answer_field="answer")` showing `get_format_str()`, `parse()`, `parse_answer()`, `format(...)`; (c) `ThinkParser(extract_fn=vf.extract_boxed_answer)`; (d) reward calculation with no model in the loop — build hand-written completions, then `asyncio.run(rubric.score_rollout(prompt=..., completion=..., answer=..., state={}))` and `score_rollouts([...])`, printing `RolloutScore.reward` and `.metrics` so weighting is visible; (e) `RubricGroup([r1, r2])` showing rewards summed and same-named metrics merged.

2) `examples/eval_gsm8k.py` — needs only an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Verified-working shape:
```python
import os
import verifiers as vf
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from verifiers.utils.data_utils import BOXED_SYSTEM_PROMPT, extract_boxed_answer, load_example_dataset

parser = vf.ThinkParser(extract_fn=extract_boxed_answer)

def correct_answer(parser, completion, answer, **kwargs) -> float:
    return 1.0 if (parser.parse_answer(completion) or "") == answer else 0.0

rubric = vf.Rubric(parser=parser,
                   funcs=[correct_answer, parser.get_format_reward_func()],
                   weights=[1.0, 0.2])
env = vf.SingleTurnEnv(eval_dataset=load_example_dataset("gsm8k", split="test").select(range(20)),
                       system_prompt=BOXED_SYSTEM_PROMPT, parser=parser, rubric=rubric)
client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=os.getenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1"),
                     api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "EMPTY"))
results = env.evaluate(client=client, model="gpt-4.1-mini", num_examples=20,
                       rollouts_per_example=1, max_concurrent=10)
print(sum(results.reward) / len(results.reward))
for name, vals in results.metrics.items():
    print(name, sum(vals) / len(vals))
env.make_dataset(results).to_json("eval_gsm8k.jsonl")
```
Keep it to v0.1.3.post0 kwargs only — `evaluate` here accepts exactly (client, model, sampling_args, num_examples, rollouts_per_example, score_rollouts, max_concurrent, **kwargs); do NOT use results_path / state_columns / save_every / interleave_scoring, which do not exist in this version.

3) `examples/multiturn_and_tools.py` — a ~30-line `MultiTurnEnv` subclass implementing the one abstract method `env_response(messages, state)` (and optionally `is_completed`, which should `return await self.max_turns_reached(state)` to keep the turn limit), plus a `vf.ToolEnv(tools=[...], max_turns=3)` using a plain Python function as a tool, both evaluated via `env.evaluate(...)`.

4) `examples/README.md` — a table stating which script needs nothing but the base install (1), which needs an endpoint (2, 3), and which needs GPUs + the `train` extra (grpo/, sft.py), plus the equivalent `vf-eval` one-liner.

findings.title: simpleqa: all three reward functions always return 0.0 (rubric.judge never awaited)
findings.detail: `JudgeRubric.judge` is `async def` (verifiers/rubrics/judge_rubric.py:58). The three reward functions in simpleqa are declared as plain `def` (lines 115, 123, 131) and call `judge_response = rubric.judge(prompt, completion, answer, state, **kwargs)` with no `await`, so `judge_response` is a coroutine object, never a string. `re.search(r"(A|B|C)", <coroutine>)` then raises TypeError. `Rubric.call_reward_func` wraps every invocation in try/except and logs+returns 0.0 on any exception (verifiers/rubrics/rubric.py:~143-148), so the failure is silent. These are the only reward functions in the environment, so correct_answer_reward_func / incorrect_answer_reward_func / not_attempted_answer_reward_func are all permanently 0.0 and the total reward is always 0.0 — the environment cannot measure anything. I reproduced the exact mechanism with a JudgeRubric and a sync reward func: the logger emits `ERROR - Error calling reward function ...: 'coroutine' object is not iterable`, a `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'JudgeRubric.judge' was never awaited`, and the returned RolloutScore is reward=0.0. Note the codebase is inconsistent here: gpqa.py:33, wiki_search.py:194 and toxicity_explanation.py:109 all correctly use `async def` + `await judge(...)`.
findings.recommendation:
Make all three `async def` and await the judge. For each of the three functions change the `def` to `async def` and the call to `await`:
```python
    async def correct_answer_reward_func(
        prompt, completion, answer, state, **kwargs
    ) -> float:
        judge_response = await rubric.judge(prompt, completion, answer, state, **kwargs)
        match = re.search(r"(A|B|C)", judge_response)
        result = match.group(0) if match else "C"
        return 1.0 if result == "A" else 0.0
```
and identically for `incorrect_answer_reward_func` (line 123, returns on "B") and `not_attempted_answer_reward_func` (line 131, returns on "C"). No other change needed — `maybe_await` in call_reward_func already handles coroutine functions.

findings.title: continuation_quality: sole reward function always returns 0.0 (rubric.judge never awaited)
findings.detail: Identical defect to simpleqa. `grade_reward` is declared `def` at line 70 and at line 71 does `judge_response = rubric.judge(prompt, completion, answer, state, **kwargs)` without `await`, yielding a coroutine. Line 73 then calls `grade_parser.parse_answer(judge_response)`; XMLParser.parse_answer (verifiers/parsers/xml_parser.py:81) takes the non-str branch and calls `self.get_assistant_messages(coroutine)`, which iterates the coroutine and raises `TypeError: 'coroutine' object is not iterable`. Rubric.call_reward_func swallows it and substitutes 0.0. `grade_reward` is registered at line 86 as the environment's ONLY reward function (weight 1.0), so the environment's reward is a constant 0.0. This is worse than a dead metric: examples/grpo/train_continuation_quality.py runs GRPO against this environment, so that shipped training example optimises against an all-zero, zero-variance reward signal. Verified by running the exact function body against a real JudgeRubric: reward=0.0 with the coroutine-never-awaited RuntimeWarning, even when the judge text contains <grade>A</grade>.
findings.recommendation:
Change line 70-71 to make the function async and await the judge:
```python
    async def grade_reward(prompt, completion, answer, state, **kwargs) -> float:
        judge_response = await rubric.judge(prompt, completion, answer, state, **kwargs)
```
The rest of the body (lines 72-84) is correct as written once `judge_response` is a real string.

findings.title: examples/sft.py crashes immediately: duplicate argparse short flag -g
findings.detail: Line 69 registers `parser.add_argument("--gradient-accumulation-steps", "-g", type=int, default=1)` and line 73 registers `parser.add_argument("--max-grad-norm", "-g", type=float, default=0.1)` — the same `-g` short option twice on the same parser. argparse raises at registration time, before any argument is parsed, so the script dies unconditionally the moment `__main__` runs, regardless of what flags the user passes. Reproduced verbatim: `argparse.ArgumentError: argument --max-grad-norm/-g: conflicting option string: -g`. This is the only non-GRPO example in the repo and it is 100% dead. I scanned every other script in examples/ and verifiers/scripts/ for duplicate short flags — sft.py is the only file affected.
findings.recommendation:
Give --max-grad-norm a free short flag. Used letters in this parser are m, d, o, n, l, b, g, r, e, w, p; `-c` is free. Change line 73 to:
```python
    parser.add_argument("--max-grad-norm", "-c", type=float, default=0.1)
```
(Alternatively drop the short flag entirely: `parser.add_argument("--max-grad-norm", type=float, default=0.1)`.) While in this file, note two harmless-but-sloppy adjacent issues worth cleaning: `--push-to-hub` (line 74) is parsed but never used because SFTConfig hardcodes `push_to_hub=True` at line 49, and line 32 rebinds the name `args` from the argparse namespace to the SFTConfig object.

findings.title: train_arc_1d.py loads the third-party reasoning_gym library instead of the reasoning_gym_env package
findings.detail: Line 24-26 calls `vf.load_environment(env_id="reasoning-gym", ...)`. `verifiers/utils/env_utils.py:load_environment` does `module_name = env_id.replace("-", "_")`, giving `reasoning_gym` — which is the name of the third-party procedural-dataset library, NOT the environment package in this repo. The environment package is environments/reasoning_gym_env/ (pyproject name `reasoning-gym-env`, module reasoning_gym_env.py), so the correct id is `reasoning-gym-env`. Because environments/reasoning_gym_env/pyproject.toml depends on `reasoning-gym`, in any real install the wrong module imports successfully and then fails the `hasattr(module, "load_environment")` check. I reproduced this with a stub `reasoning_gym` package on the path: `RuntimeError: Failed to load environment 'reasoning-gym': Module 'reasoning_gym' does not have a 'load_environment' function`. The docstring at lines 5 and 8 tells users to run `vf-install reasoning-gym` and `vf-eval reasoning-gym`, which fail the same way; environments/reasoning_gym_env/README.md:22 correctly says `vf-eval reasoning-gym-env`.
findings.recommendation:
Change the env id in all three places to `reasoning-gym-env`. Line 25:
```python
vf_env = vf.load_environment(
    env_id="reasoning-gym-env", gym="arc_1d", num_train_examples=4000, seed=1
)
```
and update the docstring to `vf-install reasoning-gym-env (-p /path/to/environments)` (line 5) and `vf-eval reasoning-gym-env (-m model_name in endpoints.py)` (line 8).

findings.title: train_arc_1d.py passes num_samples=4000, which is silently ignored
findings.detail: Same call site as the env-id bug but a distinct defect with a distinct fix. `reasoning_gym_env.load_environment` accepts (gym, num_train_examples=2000, num_eval_examples=2000, **kwargs) and `ReasoningGymEnv.__init__` accepts (gym, num_train_examples=1000, num_eval_examples=100, seed=0, **kwargs). `num_samples` is not a parameter of either, so it falls through both **kwargs chains into `Environment.__init__`, whose trailing `for key, value in kwargs.items(): setattr(self, key, value)` loop turns it into an inert instance attribute that nothing ever reads. The dataset therefore stays at the default 2000 train examples rather than the 4000 the script asks for — a silent 2x discrepancy between the script's stated intent and its behaviour. (`seed=1` in the same call IS valid: it is a real ReasoningGymEnv parameter and is forwarded correctly.)
findings.recommendation: Rename the argument to the real parameter: `num_train_examples=4000` (see the corrected call in the env-id finding above). More generally this class of silent-swallow is enabled by Environment.__init__'s setattr-everything loop; if the core team ever wants to harden it, logging a warning for unrecognised kwargs would surface exactly this bug and the summarize_text one below.

findings.title: SmolagentsToolRubric has 1 reward function but 2 weights, misaligning every tool weight
findings.detail: Lines 856-858 set `self.reward_funcs = [self.parser.get_format_reward_func()]` — exactly one entry — while lines 859-862 set `self.reward_weights = [1.0, 0.2]` — two entries. (The parent LegacyToolRubric at line 575 correctly pairs 3 funcs with 3 weights; this subclass overwrites both lists and drops a func without dropping the matching weight, evidently a copy/paste from the parent.) Line 863-864 then appends one func and one weight per tool, so the off-by-one persists: with N tools there are 1+N funcs and 2+N weights. `Rubric.score_rollout` computes the reward via `zip(reward_scores, self.get_reward_weights())`, and zip silently truncates to the shorter list, so every tool reward function is paired with the *previous* entry's weight and the final weight is discarded. I verified this with a 2-tool reproduction: the format func correctly gets 1.0, but the first tool func gets weight 0.2 when it was registered with weight=0.0, the second gets 0.0, one 0.0 weight is dropped entirely, and the total reward comes out 1.2 instead of the intended 1.0. So tool-usage metrics that are supposed to be diagnostic-only (weight 0.0) leak into the optimised reward.
findings.recommendation:
Delete the stray second weight so the two lists have equal length at line 859-862:
```python
        self.reward_weights = [
            1.0,
        ]
```
I checked every other rubric construction in environments/, examples/ and verifiers/ for funcs/weights length mismatches — this is the only one.

findings.title: README.md and docs/source/training.md use stale vf--prefixed environment ids that cannot resolve
findings.detail: The documented commands use a `vf-` prefix that no environment package in this repo carries. README.md:71 says `vf-install vf-math-python --from-repo`; README.md:209 and 212 say `vf-install vf-wordle` and `vf-eval vf-wordle`; README.md:228 and docs/source/training.md:313 show `id = "vf-math-python"`; docs/source/training.md:306 says `uv run vf-install vf-math-python --from-repo`. The actual packages are named `math-python` (environments/math_python/pyproject.toml) and `wordle` (environments/wordle/pyproject.toml). Since load_environment maps the id through `.replace("-", "_")`, `vf-wordle` resolves to a module `vf_wordle` that does not exist, so every one of these copy-pasteable commands fails. The same README file already uses the correct unprefixed form elsewhere (e.g. `vf-install gsm8k`, `vf-eval gsm8k`), so this is internal inconsistency, not a naming convention. Lower-priority instances of the same stale prefix appear inside auto-generated report blobs in environment READMEs: environments/summarize_text/README.md:50, environments/math_group/README.md:50, environments/simpleqa/README.md:54, environments/math_python/README.md:58-62 and 341-345.
findings.recommendation: Strip the `vf-` prefix in the six hand-written locations: README.md:71 -> `vf-install math-python --from-repo`; README.md:209 -> `vf-install wordle (-p /path/to/environments | --from-repo)`; README.md:212 -> `vf-eval wordle -m ...`; README.md:228 and docs/source/training.md:313 -> `id = "math-python"`; docs/source/training.md:306 -> `uv run vf-install math-python --from-repo`. The environment-README report blobs can be left alone (they are generated artefacts) or regenerated.

findings.title: summarize_text passes max_concurrent to the SingleTurnEnv constructor, where it does nothing
findings.detail: `vf.SingleTurnEnv(..., max_concurrent=10)` at line 54. `max_concurrent` is not a parameter of Environment.__init__ (its parameters are client, model, dataset, eval_dataset, system_prompt, few_shot, parser, rubric, sampling_args, message_type, oai_tools, max_workers), so it is absorbed by **kwargs and turned into an inert attribute by the setattr loop. I grepped every read of max_concurrent in verifiers/: it is only ever consumed as a call-time argument of run_rollouts, a_generate, generate and evaluate (environment.py:301, 343, 447, 497) and of Rubric.score_rollouts — nothing ever reads `self.max_concurrent` on an Environment. The concurrency limit the author intended is therefore never applied. This was the only invalid constructor kwarg found across all 33 Python files in environments/, examples/ and configs/.
findings.recommendation: Drop `max_concurrent=10` from the constructor call at line 54 and let callers pass it at evaluation time instead (`env.evaluate(client=..., model=..., max_concurrent=10)`, or `vf-eval summarize-text -c 10`). If a per-environment default is genuinely wanted, that needs a core change to have generate/evaluate fall back to a stored attribute — out of scope here and not worth it for one environment.

findings.title: numpy is imported by the vf-eval console script but is not a declared dependency
findings.detail: verifiers/scripts/eval.py does a top-level `import numpy as np`, and verifiers/utils/report_utils.py imports it too. Both are reachable from the base install: `vf-eval` is declared as a console script in [project.scripts] and is the repo's primary evaluation entry point. numpy is absent from the base `dependencies` list, so it is only present transitively via `datasets`. That happens to work today, but it is an undeclared direct dependency — if datasets ever drops or vendors its numpy requirement, `vf-eval` breaks. (Not a runtime problem right now; flagged because it is directly adjacent to the evaluation-script gap above.)
findings.recommendation: Add `"numpy",` to the base `dependencies` array in pyproject.toml, next to `"datasets"`. Purely additive; it changes no resolution outcome today since numpy is already installed transitively.

findings.title: Stray debug print statements left in two environments
findings.detail: gpqa.py:35 contains a bare `print("J")` inside the `judge_reward` reward function, so it fires once per rollout scored and spams stdout during any evaluation of that environment. xml_tool_env.py:40 contains `print(f"return_description: {return_description} ({return_type})")` inside the tool-schema construction helper, which fires once per tool at environment construction. Neither affects correctness; both are leftover debugging noise that interleaves badly with the tqdm progress bars that run_rollouts and score_rollouts render.
findings.recommendation:
Delete both lines. In gpqa.py the function then reads:
```python
    async def judge_reward(judge, prompt, completion, answer, state):
        judge_response = await judge(prompt, completion, answer, state)
        return 1.0 if "yes" in judge_response.lower() else 0.0
```
